newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada firms plan C$450 mln natural gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Canada firms plan C$450 mln natural gas pipeline.

text.p: ATCO Ltd unit CU Gas Ltd, Shell Canada Ltd and Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd said on Friday they planned to build a C$450-million Alberta pipeline to serve natural gas markets in Canada and the United States.
The companies said the Alberta Pipeline Project, under development for over a year, would pride transport for the participating companies, as well as other shippers.
Many, including Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada, have conditionally agreed to be major shippers, they said.
They said that, together, the volumes were enough for the project to proceed.

The announcement comes five days after PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd canceled plans to build its Palliser pipeline in Alberta -- which would have competed with NOVA Corp's exclusive network -- after reaching a deal for cheaper tolls on the NOVA system.

Other potential shippers on the new pipeline would have an opportunity to sign up for capacity before final design is completed, proponents said, adding that an open season would be slated for early in 1997.
The consortium said the project involved a total of 650 km of sweet gas transmission line, with diameter sizes ranging from 20 inches to 36 inches.
The APP would consist of two western pipeline legs which would originate at a number of gas plants in central Alberta and converge at the Alberta Market Centre at Carbon.
From there, the pipeline would extend east and cross the Alberta-Saskatchewan border near Empress to tie into the TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Foothills pipeline systems, they said.
The line would also access the storage facility operated by CrossAlta at Crossfield, Alberta and another operated by CU Gas at Carbon, they said.
The project will interconnect with the ATCO utility systems of Northwestern Utilities in the north near Rimbey and Canadian Western Natural Gas in the south at Carbon.
Under the agreement, CU Gas would be operator.

"The Alberta Pipeline Project will achieve significant transportation savings and cost control for producers while providing incremental capacity from Alberta," CU Gas president Larry Graburn said in a statement.
The group said the process of evaluating potential routes had begun and landowners and communities in the vicinity would be consulted.

They said the routes would mostly follow existing corridors, such as roads and utility lines. As part of the public consultation process, open houses were expected to be held in several locations in early 1997 to explain the project, receive input and respond to concerns, they said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
